answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. The opal report shows the merge explicitly at each trellis. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 205 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 18 times the capital for one share. The deposit is 8 dollars a seat. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
